title: Co–Gd phosphonate complexes as magnetic refrigerants

material_class.structural_family: distorted molecular square / rotated [4×4] Co–Gd phosphonate grid

synthesis.procedure: Compound 1 was obtained by mixing precursor 4, [Co(II)2(μ-OH2)(O2CtBu)4]·(HO2CtBu)4 (0.1 g, 0.1 mmol), Gd(NO3)3 (0.09 g, 0.2 mmol) and H2O3PtBu (0.014 g, 0.1 mmol) in MeCN (8 ml) and stirring at room temperature for a few minutes. The slurry was transferred to a 10 mL Teflon-lined autoclave, heated at 150 °C for 12 h and cooled to room temperature at 0.05 °C min−1. Purple needle-shaped crystals were collected (yield 5 mg, 4% based on 4).
synthesis.temperature: room temperature stirring, then 150 °C, cooling at 0.05 °C min−1
synthesis.time: a few minutes stirring; 12 h at 150 °C
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Purple needle-shaped crystals collected after cooling to room temperature

properties.summary: Room-temperature χMT exceeds the spin-only value because of Co(II) orbital contributions and falls to 41.5 emu K mol−1 at 2 K; low-temperature magnetization is unsaturated and exchange is predominantly antiferromagnetic. No slow magnetic relaxation is observed down to 1.8 K. The compound shows a large low-temperature magnetocaloric effect (ΔS = 20.4 J kg−1 K−1 at 4 K) and is discussed as a magnetic refrigerant.

synthesis.procedure: Compound 2 was obtained by mixing 4 (0.1 g, 0.1 mmol), 5 [Gd2(O2CtBu)6(HO2CtBu)6] (0.075 g, 0.05 mmol) and H2O3PtBu (0.014 g, 0.1 mmol) in MeCN (8 ml) and stirring at room temperature for a few minutes. The slurry was transferred to a 10 mL Teflon-lined autoclave, heated at 150 °C for 12 h and cooled to room temperature at 0.05 °C min−1. Purple needle-shaped crystals were collected (yield 75 mg, 85% based on 4).

properties.summary: χMT is above the spin-only value at room temperature and decreases to 36.1 emu K mol−1 at 2 K, consistent with predominant antiferromagnetic exchange. Magnetization at 2 K and 7 T is 39.2 μB and unsaturated. There is no slow relaxation down to 1.8 K. ΔS at 4 K is 19.9 J kg−1 K−1, supporting use as a low-temperature magnetic refrigerant.

synthesis.procedure: Compound 3 was obtained by mixing 4 (0.1 g, 0.1 mmol), 5 (0.1 g, 0.075 mmol) and H2O3PCH2Ph (0.017 g, 0.1 mmol) in MeCN (8 ml) and stirring at room temperature for a few minutes. The slurry was transferred to a 10 mL Teflon-lined autoclave, heated at 150 °C for 12 h and cooled to room temperature at 0.05 °C min−1. Purple block crystals were collected (yield 60 mg, 65% based on 5).

properties.summary: χMT falls to a minimum near 10 K and then rises sharply to 79.3 emu K mol−1 at 2 K, indicating a ferromagnetic interaction; magnetization at 2 K (46.5 μB) is closer to saturation than for 1 and 2. No slow relaxation is seen down to 1.8 K. It has the largest MCE of the series (ΔS = 22.3 J kg−1 K−1 at 4 K), attributed in part to the ferromagnetic exchange component.
